To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hASCs differentiate into CAFs under the influence of TGFβ1 and promote tumor invasion.
human adipose tissue-derived stem cells can differentiate into CAF-like cells under the impact of tumor-derived TGFβ1 and that these hASC derived CAFs can promote tumor cell invasion.
hASCs differentiate into a CAF phenotype when exposed to tumor derived factors and that these hASC-CAFs exhibit a pro-tumorigenic function, e.g. they promote tumor cell invasion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether hASCs can be a source of CACs.
the differentiation of hASCs into CAFs under the influence of TGFβ1 and the role of hASC-derived CFA-like cells in tumor invasion.
the identification and characterization of CAFs derived from hASCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
hASCs may differentiate into CAFs and that this differentiation is dependent on TFGβ1 and SDF-1 and CCL5.
adipose-derived stem cells are a potential source of carcinoma associated fibroblasts and their differentiation into CAFs is induced by tumor derived TGFβ1.
hASCs can differentiate into CAFs in response to tumor derived factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hASC-derived CACs are able to promote tumor growth and metastasis.
hASCs differentiate into CAFs under the influence of TGFβ1.
adipose tissue derived cells are recruited to the tumor microenvironment and differentiate into CAF-like cells under the control of the tumor cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hASCs may be an important source of CAF-like cells in breast cancer, and that these cells are induced by factors secreted by tumor cells.
hASC-derived CFA-like cells may contribute to tumor invasion.
adipose tissue is a rich source of cells that can be used for tissue engineering.
